newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - LIFFE agrees to buy site at edge of City.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - LIFFE agrees to buy site at edge of City.

text.p: Leading derivatives exchange LIFFE said on Monday it reached agreement to buy a site for a new trading floor at the edge of London's financial district, eschewing the up-and-coming docklands area.

LIFFE, the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange, did not disclose terms of its accord with Spitalfields Developments Limited but a spokesman said the site was chosen over five other sites, including the Canary Wharf development, in London's docklands area.

Spitalfields is an old market site on the edge of the City and next to London's working class East End. The Canary Wharf complex has been aggressively campaigning to attract financial firms and institutions and has scored some notable coups.
LIFFE said its booming business necessitated the accord.
"This agreement is made necessary by the huge growth in volumes in recent years," said LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth in a statement.

Wigglesworth, who said 1996 had beaten all previous records for business, added the exchange was gearing up for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). "We anticipate further growth in trading volumes as our EMU strategy brings more business to LIFFE," he said.
Philip Willoughby, chairman of London's Corporation City Land Committee, said the agreement was positive for the London financial district, known as the City.
"It reinforces the City's position as Europe's premier financial centre," Willoughby said. "The City needs LIFFE and LIFFE needs the City."
A LIFFE spokesman said LIFFE had been looking for a site of up to 100,000 square feet, but he said he could not comment on the size of the site in the agreement.
SDL is owned by BICC Plc, SPP Real Estate (UK) and Costain Plc.

LIFFE, which is home to some of the top European futures contracts such as the German government bond future, said it had concluded terms with City Corporation under which the City Corporation would reacquire the site if LIFFE decided not to proceed at any time prior to December 31, 2001.
The City has been battling with the Docklands area for the past few years, and both areas scored important wins at the start of the year.

In January 1996, Barclays de Zoete Wedd, the investment banking division of Barclays Plc, said it would move all its operations to the Canary Wharf office complex. But in the same month, Dutch bank ABN AMRO said it would relocate all of its London operations to a new Spitalfields office building.
